intent: Advertise and return schema-validated MCP structuredContent for every BPMN tool while preserving compatible legacy content and protocol-compliant errors.

findings.title: Imported query variants rejected by strict detail schemas
findings.resolution: Allowed finite negative imported DI coordinates and modeled evaluatesToTypeRef; both variants are exercised through the real server.

findings.title: Advertised output contracts and behavioral branches were under-pinned
findings.resolution: Pinned all 27 output schemas and exhaustively verified defaults, semantic legacy content, pagination through terminal pages, result branches, validation diagnostics, IDs, and export metadata.

findings.title: List rows and detail results shared an over-broad schema
findings.resolution: Separated strict list-row and detailed element schemas.

findings.title: Pathological hidden BPMN filenames could collapse diagram listing
findings.resolution: Kept listing processId compatible with the engine's documented empty fallback while retaining strict BPMN IDs where actual model IDs are returned.

applied_fixes: Added output schemas and parsed structured results for every advertised tool.
Preserved XML, SVG, text, and error compatibility while exposing stable machine-readable metadata and generated IDs.
Added exhaustive real-server schema/result parity with follow-on use of returned IDs.
Updated focused handler and engine expectations for the new successful result contract.
advisory_outputs: Collaboration roots continue using the engine's established processId terminology alongside an explicit type discriminator.
Output ID schemas intentionally accept valid imported NCNames beyond request-generation limits.
Malformed non-finite imported geometry remains an import-policy concern outside this output-contract bead.
Strict imported-query schemas remain hand-maintained, and no synthetic post-mutation output-validation failure is induced.
Final correctness, testing, and API-contract re-reviews reported no findings.
